title: Fitting Distribution Families with famish
text: Start loading famish core probaverse package, distionary. practice, likely just load whole probaverse library(probaverse) instead. Suppose annual streamflow maxima (cubic meters per second) 12 years. fit two distributions two different families. Fit Generalised Extreme Value (GEV) distribution maximum-likelihood estimation using wrapper: can also call fit_dst() directly use combinations. fit Log Pearson Type III distribution using L-moments log scale: fits return distionary objects, downstream probaverse tooling applies. Basic comparisons start visual diagnostics:
code: library(distionary) library(famish) x <- c(4.0, 2.7, 3.5, 3.2, 7.1, 3.1, 2.5, 5.0, 2.3, 4.5, 3.0, 3.8) gev <- fit_dst_gev(x) #> Loading required namespace: testthat gev #> Generalised Extreme Value distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>  location     scale     shape  #> 3.0658476 0.7426435 0.2699160 lp3 <- fit_dst("lp3", x, method = "lmom-log") lp3 #> Log Pearson Type III distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>   meanlog     sdlog      skew  #> 1.2652738 0.3382651 1.0430967 hist(x, freq = FALSE, ylim = c(0, 0.5), main = NULL, xlab = "Flow (cms)") plot(gev, "density", add = TRUE, n = 400, lty = 2, col = "blue4") plot(lp3, "density", add = TRUE, n = 400, lty = 3, col = "orange4") legend(   "topright",   legend = c("Data histogram", "GEV density", "LP3 density"),   lty = c(NA, 2, 3),   pch = c(15, NA, NA),   col = c("gray70", "blue4", "orange4"),   pt.cex = c(1.5, NA, NA),   bty = "n" )

title: Fitting Distribution Families with famish
text: Risk-focused work often requires tail checks. famish exposes empirical ranking quantile scores can benchmark fitted models. Return levels common periods (2-, 5-, 10-, 20-, 50-, 100-, 200-year) provide one view: Plotting empirical data fitted curves highlights tail behaviour.  Quantile scores provide quantitative metric well quantile estimated. Lower scores indicate better calibration specified quantile level (Gneiting, 2011).
code: quantiles <- enframe_return(   gev, lp3,   at = c(2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),   arg_name = "return_period",   fn_prefix = "flow" ) quantiles #> # A tibble: 7 × 3 #>   return_period flow_gev flow_lp3 #>           <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1             2     3.35     3.35 #> 2             5     4.44     4.57 #> 3            10     5.37     5.58 #> 4            20     6.45     6.70 #> 5            50     8.20     8.43 #> 6           100     9.84     9.95 #> 7           200    11.8     11.7 x_return_periods <- rpscore(x, pos = "Weibull")  plot(   sort(x_return_periods), sort(x),   xlab = "Return period (years)",   ylab = "Flow (cms)",   pch = 16, col = "black" ) lines(quantiles$return_period, quantiles$flow_gev, col = "blue4", lty = 2, lwd = 2) lines(quantiles$return_period, quantiles$flow_lp3, col = "orange4", lty = 3, lwd = 2) legend(   "topleft",   legend = c("Empirical", "GEV", "LP3"),   col = c("black", "blue4", "orange4"),   pch = c(16, NA, NA),   lty = c(NA, 2, 3),   lwd = 2,   bty = "n" ) gev_100y <- quantiles$flow_gev[quantiles$return_period == 100] lp3_100y <- quantiles$flow_lp3[quantiles$return_period == 100]  qs_gev <- quantile_score(x, gev_100y, tau = 1 - 1 / 100) qs_lp3 <- quantile_score(x, lp3_100y, tau = 1 - 1 / 100)  c(GEV = mean(qs_gev), LP3 = mean(qs_lp3)) #>        GEV        LP3  #> 0.06112929 0.06220155

title: Fitting Distribution Families with famish
text: fit_dst() dispatches different estimation routines: lmom lmom-log use lmom package (internal implementations simple families). mle uses ismev GEV, GP, Gumbel families; otherwise falls back fitdistrplus. supported methods (mge, mme) routed fitdistrplus. Wrappers fit_dst_gev() fit_dst_norm() document combinations verified extensive testing. Unsupported combinations trigger warning still attempt fitting fitdistrplus. Failure can happen data incompatible distribution (e.g., negative observations exponential fit) combination yet implemented. can control failure behaviour via: na_action: missing values handled ("null", "drop", "fail"). on_unres: distribution resolved ("null" "fail").

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: family Name target distribution family, "norm", "gev", "pois". See details. Character vector length 1. x Numeric vector containing observations fit. method Estimation method use. Valid choices include "mle", "mge", "mme", "lmom", "lmom-log". default "mle". na_action Strategy dealing NA values x. "null" returns Null distribution (distionary::dst_null()); "drop" silently removes missing observations fitting; "fail" aborts error. on_unres Behaviour distribution can resolved supplied inputs. "null" (default) yields Null distribution (distionary::dst_null()) distribution warning, whereas "fail" propagates error.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: distribution object class "dst" encapsulating fitted distribution.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: fit_dst() function currently lightweight fitting wrapper, pre-specified behaviour certain family / method combinations. full list families compatible estimation methods available via specific family wrappers, fit_dst_norm(), fit_dst_pois(), etc. fitting implemented. method = "lmom" distribution families 'gamma', 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', 'lnorm', 'norm', 'pearson3', 'weibull', 'lmom' package wrapped first calling lmom::samlmu() data vector x calculate L-moments, relevant lmom::pel*() function called estimate parameters. method = "lmom" distribution families 'exp', 'pois', 'bern', 'geom', 'chisq', 'unif', method L-moments manually implemented. families except 'unif' single parameter mean needed (thus equivalent 'mme' method). 'unif' family minimum maximum parameter values calculated l1 - 3 * l2  l1 + 3 * l2, l1 l2 first second L-moments (see Hosking, 1990, Table 1). method = "lmom-log", 'lnorm' 'lp3' families supported, otherwise distribution resolved. method fits distributions via 'lmom' method log scale. , 'norm' 'pearson3' distributions fit log data, respective 'lnorm' 'lp3' distribution obtained. method = "mle" distribution families 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', 'ismev' package used fit distribution maximum likelihood estimation. done invoking functions ismev::gev.fit(), ismev::gpd.fit() (threshold = 0), ismev::gum.fit() (respectively). method = "mle" distribution family 'bern' 'degenerate', MLE calculated manually. 'bern', parameter estimated mean 0-1 data; 'degenerate', unique data value. method = "mme" "lmom", 'cauchy' family fails fit Cauchy distributions finite moments (Feller, 1971). families 'empirical' 'finite', empirical distribution fit supplied data. 'null' family, Null distribution returned. combination family method, fitdistrplus::fitdist() function called inserting data x, family name, method. distributions require starting values parameters. families 't', 'pearson3', 'f', 'chisq', done moment matching ('mme'), 'lp3', log. 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', MLE used starting values (method = "mle"). understand distribution families , see documentation 'distionary' package dst_*() functions. example, 'lp3' family can found ?distionary::dst_lp3(). Note Gumbel distribution available yet 'distionary', simply 'gev' family shape = 0. understand estimation methods, see 'lmom' package "lmom" method. "lmom-log" method, "lmom", via log data corresponding log-transformed distributions. others, see 'fitdistrplus' package documentation.

title: Quantile score (pinball loss) — quantile_score
text: Computes asymmetric absolute loss commonly used assess quantile forecasts. Lower scores indicate better match estimated quantile observed value level tau.

title: Quantile score (pinball loss) — quantile_score
text: x Numeric vector observed values. xhat Numeric vector estimated quantiles. tau Numeric vector quantile levels (0, 1).

title: Quantile score (pinball loss) — quantile_score
text: Numeric vector quantile scores corresponding element recycled inputs.

title: Quantile score (pinball loss) — quantile_score
text: score minimises zero observation equals estimated quantile, smaller scores indicate better fitting model. Positive residuals penalised factor tau, negative residuals tau - 1. loss also known stick function, check loss, asymmetric absolute deviation, pinball loss. observation x, estimate x_hat, level tau, score (c.f. Gneiting, 2011) $$ S_\tau(x, \hat{x}) = \begin{cases}   \tau |x - \hat{x})|, & x \ge \hat{x}, \\   (1 - \tau)|x - \hat{x}|, & x < \hat{x}. \end{cases} $$ Vector recycling three arguments follows rules vctrs::vec_recycle_common().
